blocks.text: Real-world basis: Scottish blanket bogs, Okavango wetlands, floating reed islands, and Baltic raised bogs.
Landscape: Mats of peat, moss, and root systems detach and migrate across a broad shallow basin. Old Nest foundations ride on some islands; others carry only rare flowers and companion life.

Mini timeline: Era Zero — A Wild World protects slow carbon and memory processes from constant extraction. Era One — Num markets prize unpredictable island movement and turn the bog into spectacle. Era Two — Market systems are removed; water level and core peat ecologies remain. Era Three — Settlements anchor islands seasonally, then release them to avoid exhausting one basin. During Hollow Seasons, several islands repeat an old commercial route despite local currents.
Present condition: Living, mobile, and vulnerable to drying.
Corruption: 3 in route behavior; 1 in ecology.
Aesthetic brief: Copper water, green-brown floating mats, mist, low flowers, stilt markers, and distant islands moving against the wind. Show motion through displaced wakes and taut anchor lines.
Background profile: Cool; Humid; bog/wetland; patient, mobile, melancholy; very low saturated-ground friction.
